citation: Kuffour et al. (2020). Simulating coupled surface–subsurface flows with ParFlow v3.5.0: capabilities, applications, and ongoing development of an open-source, massively parallel, integrated hydrologic model. Geoscientific Model Development 13, 1373–1397.
description: ParFlow is the parallel integrated-hydrology model developed by contributors including Lawrence Livermore, Colorado School of Mines, Bonn and Berkeley. It simulates saturated or variably saturated subsurface flow and coupled overland flow, with optional land-surface processes through CLM. Users provide terrain, geology, hydraulic parameters and boundary or atmospheric forcing; outputs describe surface and subsurface water states and flows. Geographic coverage and model resolution are configurable from local domains to large watersheds. Public source and documentation are free under LGPL-2.1 terms with institutional notices and separate third-party licences. A limitation is that realistic applications need detailed input preparation and numerical configuration; the build instructions caution that some non-Linux platforms are less tested. Its coupled representation supports groundwater, irrigation and flood-infrastructure studies, complementary to Delft3D FM (model-delft3d-fm). The README cites the 2020 capabilities paper and earlier numerical-method publications. Round 1 rejected version records because their release summaries lacked explicit infrastructure terms. No hydrogeological dataset, executable or model archive was downloaded.
